title: Compose robust shear evacuations using exact diagonal contractions and small Fourier remainders
statement: For each actual calibrated inviscid shear U_l, define its exact same-input-frequency operator C_l and R_l=U_l-C_l. Every C_l(k) has operator norm<=1; for each original low Fourier mode one of nine direction pairs has a uniformly small central matrix<=eps, independently of static phase/gain/transverse errors, so ||C9(k)...C1(k)||<=eps without commuting assumptions. The accepted nearest-neighbour Dyson/ell2 bound gives ladder ell1 mass<=C*sqrt(1+s|k|)*|f_hat(k)|. Split at|k|=|p_l|/2: noncentral outputs from small inputs stay high, while H3 lattice tails control larger/resonant inputs. Thus F_-1(R_l f)<=2^24*(1+s)/|p_l|*||f||H3 for the ENTIRE Fourier series, uniformly in calibration. Selecting each N_l from the already computed previous bound K_(l-1) gives off-diagonal error<=nu/(256J),J=9. Physical stages obey u_l=C_l u_(l-1)+g_l with F_-1(g_l)<=nu/(128J), so exact telescoping u9=C9...C1u0+sum C9...C_(l+1)g_l adds critical-norm errors rather than multiplying amplification. Initial tail<=2^20*K/R^2 and low eps*K join totalerror<=nu/128 to yield F_-1(u(t9))<nu/32<nu/4 simultaneously for all initial states and calibrations. Root earlier post-release inviscid derivation proves the overlapping interface; both sources retained in this ONE operation, with no sealed independence claim.
